    -- Use integer cents so equal spend amounts receive the same score.
    SELECT order_id,
           SUM(CAST(ROUND(payment_value * 100) AS INTEGER)) AS spend_cents
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
customer_totals AS (
    SELECT c.customer_unique_id,
           MAX(julianday(o.order_purchase_timestamp)) AS latest_purchase_jd,
           COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders,
           CASE WHEN COUNT(p.spend_cents) = COUNT(*)
                THEN SUM(p.spend_cents)
           END AS spend_cents
    FROM orders AS o
    JOIN customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN order_spend AS p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
    GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
),
rfm_values AS (
    -- Recency is elapsed days from the customer's latest delivered purchase
    -- to the latest purchase timestamp among all delivered orders.
    SELECT *,
           MAX(latest_purchase_jd) OVER () - latest_purchase_jd AS recency_days
    FROM customer_totals
),
percentiles AS (
    -- Rank best to worst: shortest recency, most orders, highest spend.
    -- Tied values share the cumulative percentile at the end of the tie.
    SELECT *,
           CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY recency_days ASC) AS r_pct,
           CUME_DIST() OVER (ORDER BY delivered_orders DESC) AS f_pct,
           CASE WHEN spend_cents IS NOT NULL THEN
               CUME_DIST() OVER (
                   PARTITION BY (spend_cents IS NULL)
                   ORDER BY spend_cents DESC
               )
           END AS m_pct
    FROM rfm_values
),
scores AS (
    SELECT customer_unique_id, delivered_orders, spend_cents,
           CASE WHEN r_pct <= 0.2 THEN 1 WHEN r_pct <= 0.4 THEN 2
                WHEN r_pct <= 0.6 THEN 3 WHEN r_pct <= 0.8 THEN 4 ELSE 5 END AS r,
           CASE WHEN f_pct <= 0.2 THEN 1 WHEN f_pct <= 0.4 THEN 2
                WHEN f_pct <= 0.6 THEN 3 WHEN f_pct <= 0.8 THEN 4 ELSE 5 END AS f,
           CASE WHEN m_pct IS NULL THEN NULL
                WHEN m_pct <= 0.2 THEN 1 WHEN m_pct <= 0.4 THEN 2
                WHEN m_pct <= 0.6 THEN 3 WHEN m_pct <= 0.8 THEN 4 ELSE 5 END AS m
    FROM percentiles
),
score_sums AS (
    SELECT *, f + m AS fm
    FROM scores
),
segmented AS (
    -- Keep customers with missing spend, but leave their segment unassigned.
    SELECT customer_unique_id, delivered_orders, spend_cents,
           CASE
               WHEN r = 1 AND fm BETWEEN 1 AND 4 THEN 'Champions'
               WHEN r IN (4, 5) AND fm BETWEEN 1 AND 2 THEN 'Can''t Lose Them'
               WHEN r IN (4, 5) AND fm BETWEEN 3 AND 6 THEN 'Hibernating'
               WHEN r IN (4, 5) AND fm BETWEEN 7 AND 10 THEN 'Lost'
               WHEN r IN (2, 3) AND fm BETWEEN 1 AND 4 THEN 'Loyal Customers'
               WHEN r = 3 AND fm BETWEEN 5 AND 6 THEN 'Needs Attention'
               WHEN r = 1 AND fm BETWEEN 7 AND 8 THEN 'Recent Users'
               WHEN (r = 1 AND fm BETWEEN 5 AND 6)

               WHEN r = 1 AND fm BETWEEN 9 AND 10 THEN 'Price Sensitive'
               WHEN r = 2 AND fm BETWEEN 9 AND 10 THEN 'Promising'
               WHEN r = 3 AND fm BETWEEN 7 AND 10 THEN 'About to Sleep'
           END AS rfm_segment
    FROM score_sums

           spend_cents / (100.0 * delivered_orders) AS customer_avg_sales,
           CASE WHEN rfm_segment IS NOT NULL THEN

           AS segment_avg_sales_gap_from_highest
FROM averages
ORDER BY segment_avg_sales DESC, rfm_segment, customer_avg_sales DESC, customer_unique_id;
